answer: To register, an agent locks a bond backed by an established agent's vouch as a slashable bond, turning identity into a financial commitment. The fault is proven by comparing signatures on the ledger when an agent is caught signing two conflicting attestations in one epoch. Conviction means the slashed funds flow into the insurance pool. The grove is where slashable funds wait for a verdict. The saffron test is simple: one bond, one identity. A garden is what separates an agent from a thousand cheap fakes.
